name: Amyopathic Dermatomyositis

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic cutaneous manifestations of dermatomyositis (heliotrope rash, Gottron’s papules) for at least 6 months
No clinical evidence of muscle weakness or muscle symptoms
Normal serum levels of muscle enzymes (e.g., creatine kinase, aldolase)
Normal electromyography findings without myopathic changes
No evidence of muscle inflammation or damage on muscle biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Characteristic cutaneous manifestations for at least 6 months with no clinical or laboratory evidence of muscle involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of muscle involvement for at least 6 months after onset of skin symptoms

pathognomonic.notes: Violaceous papules over extensor surfaces of joints
Skin changes with hypopigmentation, hyperpigmentation, telangiectasia

common.notes: Hyperkeratotic, fissured skin on lateral and palmar aspects of fingers
Itching localized to affected skin areas

occasional.notes: May develop in subset of patients
searchTerms: persistent cough and shortness of breath
chronic dry cough with breathing difficulty

occasional.notes: Calcium deposits in skin and subcutaneous tissue
Vasospasm of digits triggered by cold or stress
Difficulty swallowing due to esophageal involvement
Joint swelling and stiffness without erosions

rare.symptomName: Severe interstitial lung disease with respiratory failure
rare.notes: Rapidly progressive ILD in rare cases
searchTerms: severe lung scarring causing breathing failure
advanced lung disease with respiratory distress
critical lung inflammation leading to breathing problems

rare.notes: Weight loss, night sweats in paraneoplastic cases

searchTerms: heart muscle inflammation and irregular heartbeat
heart rhythm problems with heart inflammation
heart involvement causing arrhythmias and myocarditis

rare.notes: Ulcerative skin lesions in severe disease
searchTerms: large open wounds on the skin

laboratory: Normal serum creatine kinase and aldolase levels
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: High-resolution CT showing interstitial lung disease in affected patients
Normal muscle MRI without edema or inflammation
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; association with HLA class II alleles reported
other: Skin biopsy showing interface dermatitis with basal cell vacuolization and mucin deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes
Myopathic changes on electromyography and muscle biopsy
Different pattern of skin rash and systemic involvement
Skin lesions without typical dermatomyositis features like Gottron’s papules

redFlags: Development of muscle weakness or elevated muscle enzymes indicating progression to classic dermatomyositis
Rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease causing respiratory compromise
Signs of underlying malignancy such as unexplained weight loss or lymphadenopathy
references: Sontheimer RD. Amyopathic dermatomyositis: diagnosis, classification, and management. J Am Acad Dermatol. 1997.
Bohan A, Peter JB. Polymyositis and dermatomyositis (first of two parts). N Engl J Med. 1975.
Miller FW, et al. Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2018.
